questions.q: Why does star topology dominate modern wired networks?
options: It was the first topology ever invented
A single cable failure only takes down the one device on that cable, not the whole network
It requires no central switch
It's the cheapest possible topology to cable
questions.explain: Star topology's key advantage is fault isolation — a broken cable only affects the one device on it, unlike bus or ring topologies where a single break can disrupt the whole network.

questions.q: What is the main weakness of star topology?
options: The central switch is a single point of failure
It can't support more than 5 devices
It doesn't support wireless devices
It requires fiber optic cable exclusively
questions.explain: Because every device connects through one central switch, that switch becomes a single point of failure — production networks address this with redundant switches and uplinks.

questions.q: Why does a full mesh topology not scale well cabling-wise?
options: Mesh requires exactly one connection per device regardless of size
Mesh topology can only use wireless, never cable
The number of connections needed grows rapidly — a full mesh of 10 devices needs 45 connections
Mesh topology is illegal in most data centers
questions.explain: A full mesh connects every device to every other device directly, so connection count grows combinatorially — 10 devices already need 45 individual connections.

questions.q: What does twisting the pairs in twisted-pair copper cable actually accomplish?
options: It is purely cosmetic and has no electrical function
It converts electrical signals into light
It increases the cable's maximum physical length indefinitely
It cancels out electromagnetic interference between the pairs
questions.explain: The twisting in twisted-pair cable cancels electromagnetic interference between the wire pairs, which is a key reason it performs as well as it does for its cost.

questions.q: Why does fiber optic cable support much longer distances than twisted-pair copper?
options: Fiber distance limits are identical to copper's roughly 100-meter limit
Fiber uses the same signaling method as copper but at a lower voltage
Fiber carries data as light pulses, which aren't subject to electromagnetic interference the way electrical signals are
Fiber is simply thicker than copper
questions.explain: Because fiber transmits light rather than electrical signals, it isn't subject to electromagnetic interference, allowing usable distances of kilometers instead of copper's roughly 100-meter limit.
